documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
42F graphic designer transferring care; liked the idea of being able to text her doctor. Prior office records reviewed (filed 7/8).

Hypothyroidism: on levothyroxine 75 mcg for years, takes it first thing with water, coffee 30-40 min later. Energy fine, no cold intolerance, no constipation, periods regular. Last TSH 2023 in range per old records.

Weight: has carried extra weight since her late 20s. Mostly desk-bound for work; walks on weekends, tried a few apps. Wants to work on it but not interested in medication right now.

PMH: hypothyroidism, obesity.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 7; cholecystectomy ~2017.
Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg qAM.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother hypothyroid; father type 2 DM.
SH: never smoker, a glass of wine or two a week, no drugs. Works from a home studio and some days in an office in town.

ROS: negative for chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, GI or GU complaints, rash, numbness, mood change.

EXAM
Vitals as recorded; BMI about 34.
Well-appearing, pleasant. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, well-healed small surgical scars. No edema. Affect bright. PHQ-2 0.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Hypothyroidism - clinically euthyroid. Continue levothyroxine 75 mcg. TSH today.
2. Obesity, BMI ~34 - talked through small steps: a lunchtime walk, fewer evening snacks, aiming for 5% over a year. A1c and lipids today given her dad's diabetes.
3. Health maintenance - HIV and hep C screens once, today. Mammogram ordered (none since turning 40). Pap/HPV 2022 normal, next 2027. Tdap 2019. Flu and COVID this fall.

RTC for a physical next summer, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tracy, everything from Tuesday is back and normal: thyroid level right where it should be on your current dose, blood sugar/A1c in the normal range, cholesterol fine for your risk (LDL flags just over the lab's cutoff, nothing to treat), kidney and liver tests and blood counts normal, HIV and hepatitis C screens negative. No changes. The mammogram order is in; scheduling should reach out, or you can call them directly.

reports.text: Technique: bilateral digital screening mammography with tomosynthesis, standard CC and MLO views. No prior studies available for comparison. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast. Skin and nipples unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Routine annual screening recommended.

documents.body: Your screening mammogram from Tuesday was read as negative, nothing of concern. Next one is due in about a year. -RN for the PCP

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 7 wks of pins-and-needles in the R hand, mostly thumb through ring finger. Worst at night, shakes the hand out to get back to sleep. Notices it after long sessions on the tablet and mouse. No neck pain, no fall or injury, L hand fine. Thyroid meds unchanged.

O: Vitals as charted. Neck nontender, full ROM, no pain with rotation. R hand: reports reduced feel at the thumb and index fingertips to light touch. Skin normal, no swelling.

A/P: R hand paresthesias, median-nerve pattern most likely. Neurology referral placed for evaluation. In the meantime, keep the wrist straight while working, take breaks.
Flu and updated COVID vaccine given today, tolerated.
TSH was normal in July.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/21/2024
Reason for referral: right hand sensory symptoms (referred by her primary care physician)

HISTORY
Ms. Hanlon is a 42-year-old right-handed graphic designer who has had steadily increasing numbness and tingling in the right hand over roughly three months. She describes intermittent burning and pins and needles in the thumb, index and middle fingers and the thumb side of the ring finger. Symptoms are worse overnight and occasionally wake her. Over the past few weeks she has been dropping things more often, which she has noticed at her drawing desk. The symptoms are getting in the way of her work at the keyboard and tablet. She has had no neck pain, injury, or weakness in the left arm.

Past history: hypothyroidism, obesity. Surgeries: tonsillectomy in childhood, cholecystectomy.
Medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: hypothyroidism in her mother; type 2 diabetes in her father.
Social: never smoker; drinks socially, one or two a week.

EXAMINATION
Alert, fluent, cranial nerves normal. Right hand: diminished light touch and pinprick over the palmar thumb and index finger. Mild flattening of the thenar eminence. Weakness of right thumb abduction and opposition. Tinel sign at the wrist and Phalen maneuver did not reproduce symptoms. Strength, tone, reflexes and sensation otherwise normal in all four limbs; gait and coordination normal.

IMPRESSION
Right carpal tunnel syndrome, with sensory loss in the median distribution and early thenar involvement.

RECOMMENDATIONS
- Neutral-position wrist splint at night.
- Workstation changes: keyboard and mouse at elbow height, wrist kept straight, short breaks every hour.
- Return or contact us if symptoms progress.

Thank you for this referral.
Outpatient neurology

documents.title: Wrist brace
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - the neurologist said to wear a wrist splint at night. Does it matter which one? The drugstore has like six kinds. Also wondering if I need a prescription for insurance.

documents.title: RE: Wrist brace
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Look for one with a stiff bar on the palm side that holds the wrist flat, not bent back. An over-the-counter one is fine and usually cheaper than going through insurance. Wear it every night for at least a few weeks before judging it. Let me know how it goes.
